title: Building a Cloud Data Lake (S3 + Glue/Lake Formation)

scenes.title: Building a Cloud Data Lake
scenes.narration: A cloud data lake stores raw and refined data in object storage, with a catalog and governance layer that makes it queryable and secure.

scenes.title: The Core Components
bullets: Object storage like S3 holds data cheaply across raw, cleaned, and curated zones.
A data catalog such as AWS Glue tracks table schemas and partitions.
A governance layer like Lake Formation enforces fine-grained permissions on the data.
scenes.narration: A data lake begins with cheap object storage organized into zones from raw to curated. A catalog like Glue records the schemas and partitions so query engines know how to read the files. A governance layer such as Lake Formation then applies fine-grained access control across it all.

scenes.title: The Medallion Layout
scenes.narration: A widely used pattern organizes the lake into progressive layers. The bronze zone holds raw data exactly as ingested, the silver zone cleans and conforms it, and the gold zone contains business-ready aggregates. Each layer serves a purpose, and moving data through them keeps quality visible and reprocessing simple.

scenes.title: Cataloging Data with a Glue Crawler
scenes.code:
aws glue create-crawler \
  --name raw-sales-crawler \
  --role AWSGlueServiceRole \
  --database-name data_lake \
  --targets '{"S3Targets": [{"Path": "s3://my-lake/bronze/sales/"}]}'

aws glue start-crawler --name raw-sales-crawler
scenes.narration: A Glue crawler automatically discovers the schema of files in a lake path. Here we create a crawler pointed at the bronze sales prefix and tell it which catalog database to populate. Running the crawler infers columns and partitions, after which query engines like Athena can read the data as an ordinary table.

scenes.title: Data Lake vs. Data Warehouse
scenes.narration: A data lake accepts any file format and applies schema only when you read, giving cheap flexibility. A warehouse enforces structure on write and optimizes heavily for query speed. Many modern platforms combine both, landing raw data in the lake and serving refined data through the warehouse.

scenes.text: A cloud data lake pairs cheap object storage with a catalog and governance — organize it into clear zones and it becomes the flexible heart of your platform.
scenes.narration: A well-run data lake combines inexpensive storage with a catalog and access controls. Organizing it into clear bronze, silver, and gold zones turns raw files into a governed, queryable foundation for the whole platform.
